content: This brief work extends the permanental process model to incorporate fixed effects. By assigning a prior to the fixed effects coefficients, we demonstrate that, as the prior becomes increasingly non-informative, the intensity function of the permanental process can be derived using the representer theorem. This results in a natural decomposition into a fixed effects component and a function belonging to a Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space (RKHS). We further show that the limiting equivalent kernel defines an RKHS whose squared norm precisely corresponds to the limiting penalty. This framework offers a clear scientific interpretation of permanental process models and facilitates the integration of domain knowledge into the estimation procedure.

"""
This brief work extends the permanental process model to include fixed effects. By placing a prior on the fixed effects coefficients, we show that, as the prior becomes increasingly non-informative, the intensity function of the permanental process can be derived via the representer theorem. This leads to a natural decomposition into a fixed effects term and a function residing in a Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space (RKHS). We further demonstrate that the limiting equivalent kernel defines an RKHS whose squared norm exactly matches the limiting penalty. This framework provides a clear scientific interpretation of permanental process models and enables the incorporation of domain knowledge into the estimation procedure.
